result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.has_node()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if a node exists in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L3485-L3529){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.has_node(node) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Verifies whether a node (specified by ID or label) exists in the graph. Returns `False` for invalid inputs or missing nodes. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node ID (int) or label (str) to check. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the node exists, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Both node IDs and labels work as lookups, and unknown identifiers return `False` rather than raising: ::: {#4e0eac82 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="Alice") .add_node(label="Bob") ) ( graph.has_node("Alice"), graph.has_node(1), graph.has_node("Charlie"), graph.has_node(999), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, True, False, False) ``` ::: :::
